source: Bereshit Rabbah 17:3; Yevamot 63a:3
claim_en: כְּנֶגְדּוֹ (kenegdo) - the paradox word of the helper-plan - stands in the Torah exactly twice, at our 2:18 and our 2:20, and BOTH are written with the identical consonants. R. Elazar reads the one spelling two ways: vocalized kenegdo it means 'alongside him, for him'; vocalized ke-negdo it means 'AGAINST him, striking him'. Bereshit Rabbah 17:3 gives the rule the two vocalizations encode: if he merits, she is a helper; if he does not, she is against him. One ink, two states, decided by conduct.

source: Yevamot 61b:16; Ketubot 67b:2; Tosefta Ketubot 6:9; Tosefta Peah 4:10; Sifrei Devarim 116:18
claim_en: The first NEGATIVE verdict in the corpus - לֹא טוֹב (lo tov, 'it is NOT GOOD that the man be alone', our 2:18) - is read as installing a standing obligation, not describing a mood: Shmuel rules that even one who already has children may not remain without a wife. And the same verse's little word לוֹ (lo, 'for him') carries a CHARITY law by explicit wording-analogy at two tannaitic seats: the orphan's maintenance, 'sufficient for his deficiency... for HIM' (Deuteronomy 15:8), includes a WIFE - 'just as lo there is a wife, so lo here' - so the community marries him off on our token's strength, and the orphan girl is married off first, 'a woman's shame being greater than a man's'.

check.note: Two laws - a standing marital obligation and a charity measure - derived from one verdict operator's own words.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 17:5
claim_en: תַּרְדֵּמָה (tardemah, 'deep slumber') stands in the Torah exactly twice: our 2:21, the surgery, and Genesis 15:12, where it falls on Abram before the covenant vision. Bereshit Rabbah 17:5 types the word into three kinds - the slumber of SLEEP (our verse is the type-specimen), the slumber of PROPHECY (Abram's), and the slumber of TRANCE (1 Samuel 26:12, outside the Torah) - so the Torah holds exactly the first two seats and the third lies beyond this corpus. The same passage sets three microcosms beside it: sleep a sixtieth of death, dream a sixtieth of prophecy, the Sabbath a sixtieth of the world to come.

source: Eruvin 18a:15; Berakhot 61a:15; Berakhot 61a:16

Both the closing-of-the-flesh and the building operators are read as the dispute's exhibits: on the side-reading the open flank needed closing and little needed building; on the tail-reading a whole new structure was built.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 18:1; Niddah 45b:11; Shabbat 95a:1; Ketubot 8a:3
claim_en: Three things ride the build operator of our 2:22, וַיִּבֶן (va-yiven, 'and He built'). A LAW OF LEGAL CAPACITY: the word is read as בִּינָה (binah, 'understanding') granted her in greater measure, and Rav Chisda gives this as Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's stated REASON for examining a girl's vows a year earlier than a boy's. A SHABBAT LABOR CATEGORY: braiding hair counts as BUILDING, because the Holy One braided her hair and brought her to the man - the labor joining the thirty-nine-category system this corpus tracks from day seven. And STANDING LITURGY: the third wedding blessing quotes this operator, 'out of His very self He formed a building for eternity'.

check.note: One operator grounding a capacity law, a Sabbath labor category, and a standing blessing.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 18:4
claim_en: THE SACRED-TONGUE PROOF, resting on our naming operator. At 2:23 the man names her אִשָּׁה (isha, 'woman') and gives the reason - כִּי מֵאִישׁ לֻקֳחָה ('for from אִישׁ (ish, MAN) was she taken'). The name and its stated derivation correspond only in Hebrew; in Greek and Aramaic the pair fails. From this the chain draws a conclusion about the corpus itself: the Torah was given in the sacred tongue and THE WORLD WAS CREATED in the sacred tongue - the naming operator's internal consistency taken as evidence about the language of creation.

check.note: Verified in the ink at derivation: Genesis 2:23 carries אשה at word 10 and מאיש at word 12, the pair the argument stands on. The cross-language claim itself is outside a Torah-only corpus and is therefore not machine-checkable.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 18:5; Sanhedrin 58a:8; Sanhedrin 58a:7; Sanhedrin 57b:10; Sanhedrin 58b:14; Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:1:13; Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 11:2:6
claim_en: THE SPAN'S LAW CROWN. Our 2:24 pattern operator - a man leaves father and mother, cleaves to his wife, and they become one flesh - is the source of the family law binding all humanity, read clause by clause: 'shall CLEAVE' excludes a male; 'to HIS WIFE' excludes another man's wife; 'ONE FLESH' excludes animals, with which flesh cannot become one. The GENDER SCOPE is settled from the tail clause - 'a man shall leave' might have exempted the woman, but 'they shall be one flesh' combines them, binding both. The manner of cleaving is itself actionable. And the leave-clause's referents are disputed at the Babylonian seat: R. Eliezer reads 'his father' as the father's sister and 'his mother' as the mother's sister; R. Akiva reads 'his father' as the father's WIFE and 'his mother' literally - each token of our verse assigned disputed legal referents, carried dual-track.

check.note: The unit's pattern operator read as a statute with scope, exclusions, and a recorded referent dispute.
